 ‘Today’ star Willie Geist announces major new career move: ‘Bittersweet goodbye’ 
 By 
 Riley Cardoza 
 Published 
 Nov. 16, 2026, 7:22 a.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make Page Six a Preferred Source 
 Willie Geist’s time at “Morning Joe” is coming to an end after nearly two decades at the helm of the MS NOW show.
 Instead, the journalist will focus full-time on “Sunday Today with Willie Geist” in 2027 — and, per a press release Monday morning, “broaden his presence across ‘Today’ and other NBC News platforms.”
 He gushed, “I am so grateful to both NBC and MSNOW for the unique opportunity to do what I love at both networks.”

 Geist, 51, called the transition “bittersweet” as he bid “goodbye to Joe [Scarborough], Mika [Brzezinski] and the place that made possible everything else in [his] career over the last two decades.”
 He continued, “I am thrilled to settle in with my family at ‘Today’ and dedicate all of my time to that special place.”
 On air, he reminded viewers that when MSNBC became MS NOW, he was “flattered” to be the only employee allowed to straddle both networks.
 8

 8 
 Geist, pictured speaking onstage during a Parkinson’s research fundraiser in New York City on Nov. 14, 2026, said it was “never intended” that he would straddle MS Now and NBC News “forever.” Getty Images for The Michael J. Fox Foundation

 “It was never intended to last forever,” he said. “And so, it is with a very heavy heart — heavy with memories, experiences, and friends and family like the two people on the screen with me now — that I announce my run on ‘Morning Joe’ will end next month.”
 The Emmy nominee dubbed the career update “surreal.”
 Geist’s co-hosts, notably, announced in March that they are under contract with MS Now through 2029.
 8 
 He has co-hosted “Morning Joe” since 2007 with Mika Brzezinski and Joe Scarborough, pictured above broadcasting live from Crenshaw High School in 2021. NBCUniversal via Getty Images 
 8 
 Geist, pictured on the set of NBC’s “Today” show in June 2010, joined “Today” as a co-host two years later. NBC Newswire/NBCUniversal via Getty Images 
 Scarborough, 63, and Brzezinski, 59, have co-hosted “Morning Joe” with Geist since its start in 2007.
 The simultaneously “proud” and “sad” duo gushed during Monday’s show about how “grateful” they are to have worked with Geist.
 “We knew it was coming after the midterms,” Scarborough acknowledged. “We had some really emotional conversations. I’m getting emotional right now. We shared our lives together.”
 8 
 “Sunday TODAY with Willie Geist,” pictured above in July 2019, started in 2016. NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images 
 Mentioning the “corporate overlords,” Scarborough added, “I’m not thrilled, you’re not thrilled and Mika’s not thrilled. … We knew it was coming to an end. It doesn’t make it any easier, but again we’re so grateful.”
 Brzezinski, for her part, reminded Geist that she “always told” him, “You have a big future beyond us.”
 She reflected on their time together as being “sweet, fun [and] remarkable.”
 8 
 Geist, pictured with Savanah Guthrie and Natalia Dyer on “Today” in August 2019, called his career move a “surreal” one. NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal via Getty Images 
 The pair clarified that Geist will take part in the 20th anniversary celebration of “Morning Joe” in May.
 Geist was five years into his time on the talk show when he joined “Today” in 2012 as a co-host — and, in 2016, he started “Sunday Today.”
 Additionally, he hosts the “Sunday Sitdown” podcast and contributes to NBC Sports.
